newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures mixed, distant months dip.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures mixed, distant months dip.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures settled mixed on Tuesday, as selling gathered force late in the day on the yen's rebound against the dollar, traders said.
Prices ranged from 100 yen per tonne lower to 220 yen higher. The benchmark March 1998 contract ended down 100 yen at 15,840 yen. Daily volume was estimated at 76,150 lots.

The market started sharply higher, following gains in the Chicago market overnight. "In the late afternoon session, the yen's rebound prompted investors to take profits, especially in distant months," one trader said.
The focus is on a USDA report to be released on Wednesday.

Traders predicted there would be little change in corn demand/supply figures in the USDA report. "The market is watching figures of U.S. soybean inventories and how they will affect corn futures in the Chicago market," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
The spot March contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $3.11 per bushel at 0845 GMT, compared with Monday's close of $3.12.
The CBOT soybean futures spot March contract was at $8.59-1/2 at 0845 GMT, up from $8.57-3/4 at Monday's close.
